words.sense: To formally deny connection or responsibility.
words.concise_meaning: To claim 'that isn't mine' or 'I don't know them'.
misconceptions: Thinking it means 'to dislike' or 'to disagree with'.

words.sense: To reject validity, truth, or obligation.
words.concise_meaning: To claim 'that is false' or 'that is not binding'.
misconceptions: Thinking it means 'to ignore' or 'to forget'.

semantic_axes.description: Denying a personal connection (disavow) vs. rejecting the truth/validity of a thing (repudiate).
Protecting own reputation (disavow) vs. asserting moral/logical superiority (repudiate).

edge.boundary_rule: If you deny owning or knowing it, disavow; if you reject it as false or wrong, repudiate.

misconceptions.M1: Confusing 'I'm not related' (disavow) with 'this claim is wrong' (repudiate).
misconceptions.M2: Assuming both words mean 'to not like something'.
misconceptions.M3: Thinking repudiate is only for legal situations.

disavow: The mayor had to disavow the statement made by his campaign manager.
She publicly disavowed any knowledge of the secret meeting.
The company was forced to disavow the rogue employee's actions.
After the controversy, he decided to disavow his former mentor.
The agency will disavow all involvement if the mission fails.
They quickly disavowed the flyer that was distributed in their name.
repudiate: The professor decided to repudiate the outdated study.
The government chose to repudiate the trade agreement signed years ago.
She felt compelled to repudiate the false accusations made against her.
The court will likely repudiate the claim due to lack of evidence.
He formally repudiated the findings of the report.
The organization must repudiate these discriminatory practices.

disavow: She repudiated the idea that the earth was flat.
He disavowed the contract because it was signed under pressure.
The jury repudiated the defendant's testimony as entirely fabricated.
The country disavowed the international treaty on human rights.
The committee repudiated the candidate due to their past behavior.
repudiate: The bank repudiated the client's credit card transaction.
She repudiated her own cousin after the incident.
He repudiated his own signature on the document.
The board disavowed the proposed changes to the bylaws.
The firm repudiated the software developer who caused the bug.

borderline.text: The scientist was forced to [blank] the data, as it was clearly tampered with.
borderline.note: While one could disavow the data (deny its connection to their work), repudiate is stronger because it asserts the data's invalidity.

borderline.text: The senator had to [blank] his own past comments that were becoming a liability.
borderline.note: He is denying his connection to those comments (disavow), but could also repudiate them if he's saying they were fundamentally wrong.

borderline.text: The debtor attempted to [blank] the loan agreement, claiming he didn't understand the terms.
borderline.note: Rejecting the binding nature of the agreement.

borderline.text: The leader was quick to [blank] the radical group, stating they did not represent his movement.

chains.frame: What the minister did to the scandal: ___

beats.text: The minister said he had never met the lobbyist.
Evidence showed they had lunch together. The minister still says they don't know each other.

chains.feedback_short: He is denying a connection to the lobbyist.
chains.feedback_deep: The word disavow is perfect for denying personal or professional connection. Even when evidence suggests otherwise, the act remains a disavowal, not a rejection of validity.
chains.contrast_rule: Disavow = Deny connection; Repudiate = Reject validity.
chains.hint: Focus on whether he's saying it isn't true or saying he isn't involved.

chains.frame: The CEO's view on the leaked memo: ___

beats.text: The CEO stated that the leaked memo did not come from his office.
The CEO later acknowledged it came from his office, but called its claims completely false.
beats.reason: Now rejecting the validity of the content.

chains.feedback_short: He stopped denying origin and started rejecting the validity of the content.
chains.feedback_deep: The CEO initially denied the memo's origin (disavow). When he acknowledged it was from his office, his new action was to declare its claims false (repudiate).
chains.hint: Did he change his mind about where it came from or what it says?

chains.frame: The professor's stance on the study: ___

beats.text: The professor did not want to be associated with the experimental findings.
The findings were later proven to be based on completely flawed methodology, so the professor distanced himself further.

chains.feedback_short: He is focused on distancing himself, not necessarily judging the validity.
chains.feedback_deep: While the methodology was flawed, the professor's *primary* action is distancing himself from the association, making disavow the narrower, better fit.
chains.hint: Is he focusing on his own reputation or the study's scientific quality?

chains.frame: Maya's attitude is ___

beats.text: Maya claimed she had no hand in the team's project failure.
She insisted that the failure was entirely due to management decisions.

chains.feedback_short: She is still just denying her involvement.
chains.feedback_deep: Even though she blamed management, her core act remains denying her own connection to the failure. This is a false shift — the motivation didn't change.
chains.contrast_rule: Distraction is not a semantic shift.
chains.hint: Does her blaming management change her relationship to her own involvement?

chains.frame: The king's act is ___

beats.text: The king claimed he had never promised the land to the lords.
In fact, the promise was made in an ancient decree that the king now says is not binding.
beats.reason: Reframing as rejecting a legal obligation.

chains.feedback_short: He stopped denying the act and started rejecting the validity of the decree.
chains.feedback_deep: Initially, he denied the promise existed (disavow). The situation is reframed when it's revealed the promise exists but is now considered invalid (repudiate).
chains.hint: Is he saying 'I didn't do it' or 'that law is not valid'?

chains.frame: The company's position on the debt: ___

beats.text: The company stated the debt was never legally binding.
They presented documents showing the contract was forged.

chains.feedback_short: They are consistently rejecting the validity of the contract.
chains.feedback_deep: The company is not denying connection to the debt; they are asserting the contract itself is invalid due to forgery. Repudiate fits perfectly for rejecting validity.
chains.hint: Are they saying 'I didn't sign it' (disavow) or 'the contract itself is not valid' (repudiate)?

chains.frame: The philosopher's treatment of the doctrine: ___

beats.text: He claimed he had never followed that school of thought.
However, he admitted his earlier work relied on it, but insisted the doctrine itself is logically incoherent.
beats.reason: Now rejecting the validity of the doctrine.

chains.feedback_short: He shifted from denying his connection to attacking the doctrine's validity.
chains.feedback_deep: He first claimed no connection (disavow). When the connection was established, his focus shifted to the doctrine's flawed logic (repudiate).
chains.hint: Is he focusing on his own history or the doctrine's merit?

chains.frame: The manager's act is ___

beats.text: The manager refused to support the new policy.
She specifically stated the policy is structurally harmful to the company.

chains.feedback_short: She is rejecting the policy's validity, which is more precise.
chains.feedback_deep: While 'refused to support' could be ambiguous, 'structurally harmful' makes it clear she is rejecting its validity, a core feature of repudiate.
chains.hint: Is she saying 'I don't support it' or 'this is fundamentally invalid'?

chains.frame: The journal's decision on the paper: ___

beats.text: The journal stated they were not responsible for the author's personal views.
They then published a note saying the author's data was manipulated and therefore the paper is entirely without merit.
beats.reason: Corrupted into a rejection of validity.

chains.feedback_short: They moved from denying responsibility to rejecting the paper's scientific merit.
chains.feedback_deep: The journal's first act was distancing (disavow). The second act was a formal rejection of scientific validity (repudiate).
chains.hint: Are they saying 'not our view' or 'not valid science'?

chains.frame: The critic's view of the book: ___

beats.text: The critic refused to accept the premise of the novel.
Upon further reflection, the critic admitted the premise, while radical, successfully illustrated the character's journey.
beats.reason: Rehabilitating the premise — wait, the word should be abandoned.

chains.feedback_short: This context doesn't fit the pair well; please re-examine.
chains.feedback_deep: Rehabilitation here shows how the critic stopped repudiating the premise and instead accepted it.
chains.hint: The critic stopped rejecting the premise.

chains.frame: What Sarah did to her ex: ___

beats.text: Sarah told everyone she had never dated the guy.
When someone showed her a photo of them together, she said it was a fake.

chains.feedback_short: She is persistently denying the relationship.
chains.feedback_deep: Sarah's action is consistently about denying a personal connection, making disavow the correct choice.
chains.hint: Is she rejecting a fact or denying a personal link?

chains.frame: The athlete's reaction to the coach's claim: ___

beats.text: The athlete said the coach never told him to cheat.
The athlete later realized the instruction was indeed given, but added that such instruction is completely against the spirit of the sport.
beats.reason: Rejecting the validity of the instruction.

chains.feedback_short: He stopped denying the instruction and started attacking its moral validity.
chains.feedback_deep: First, he denied the connection/instruction (disavow). When the instruction was proven, he attacked the validity of the instruction itself (repudiate).
chains.hint: Is he saying 'I didn't receive that' or 'that is morally wrong'?

chains.frame: The travel agency's stance on the policy: ___

beats.text: The agency says the airline's claim about overbooking fees is entirely false.
They produced internal documents showing the airline's fee structure was illegal under current regulations.

chains.feedback_short: They are consistently rejecting the airline's claims as false.
chains.feedback_deep: The agency is rejecting the validity of the airline's claims based on legality, not denying their own involvement.
chains.hint: Are they saying 'we aren't involved' or 'that statement is false'?

chains.frame: What Tom did to the broken vase: ___

beats.text: Tom said he had never even seen the vase before.
Even when shown a video of him holding it, he insisted it wasn't him.

chains.feedback_short: He is consistently denying any personal connection to the vase.
chains.feedback_deep: Tom is denying his connection to the object (the vase). He is not questioning the validity of the vase, so disavow is the clear choice.
chains.hint: Is he rejecting a fact or denying a personal link?

chains.frame: The artist's view of the critic: ___

beats.text: The artist said he had no working relationship with the critic.
Actually, they had worked together, but the artist argued the critic's review is totally baseless.
beats.reason: Now rejecting the validity of the critic's words.

chains.feedback_short: He moved from denying a connection to rejecting the validity of the critic's words.
chains.feedback_deep: He first denied the relationship (disavow). When proven wrong, he shifted to attacking the critic's argument as baseless (repudiate).
chains.hint: Is he denying a personal connection or attacking an idea?

chains.frame: The group's position on the practice: ___

beats.text: The group said they did not authorize the secret activity.
They then admitted they had authorized it, but now argue it is unethical and they should have never allowed it.
beats.reason: Now rejecting the validity/morality of the act.

chains.feedback_short: They moved from denying responsibility to condemning the ethical validity of the act.
chains.feedback_deep: First, they denied their involvement (disavow). Then, they condemned the moral validity of the practice (repudiate).
chains.hint: Are they denying responsibility or judging an action's morality?

chains.frame: The boss's response to the error: ___

beats.text: The boss said that the error was not part of his original plan.
Even after it was shown that he signed off on the plan, he insisted that the execution was completely his team's fault.
beats.reason: Still denying his own connection to the error.

chains.feedback_short: He is persistently denying his personal involvement in the error.
chains.feedback_deep: The boss is consistently trying to deny his own connection to the error, making disavow the right choice.
chains.hint: Is he rejecting an idea or denying his personal involvement?

chains.frame: The city's position on the tax: ___

beats.text: The city council claimed they had no knowledge of the tax hike.
They later realized they had passed it, but now argue it was a poor decision that needs to be reversed.
beats.reason: Still fundamentally about distancing themselves from the initial act.

chains.feedback_short: They are still focused on distancing themselves from their initial action.
chains.feedback_deep: Even after acknowledging their role, their focus remains on distancing themselves from the initial decision, a false shift.
chains.hint: Does their change in tone mean they are rejecting validity or just distancing?

chains.frame: The author's view on the theory: ___

beats.text: The author argued the theory is based on a misunderstanding of the original text.
He further argued that the theory is not just wrong, but fundamentally destructive to the field of study.
beats.reason: Narrowing the focus to the theory's impact.

chains.feedback_short: He is consistently rejecting the theory's validity and impact.
chains.feedback_deep: The author is consistently attacking the theory, so repudiate is the appropriate and stable choice as the argument becomes more specific.
chains.hint: Are they denying their own connection or attacking an idea?

chains.frame: The company's response to the criticism: ___

beats.text: The company said the criticism does not reflect their core values.
They added that the criticism is based on an outdated understanding of their business model.

chains.feedback_short: They are persistently denying their alignment with the criticism.
chains.feedback_deep: The company is distancing its values from the criticism, making disavow the consistent choice, even as they provide more context.
chains.hint: Are they denying alignment or judging validity?
